question:
A 30-year-old gravida 4, para 3 woman is in active labor following spontaneous rupture of membranes
at 39 weeks' gestation. She has a history of three uncomplicated vaginal deliveries, with the largest
infant weighing approximately 8 pounds. An epidural is placed, and the patient is comfortable. Her
cervical examination reveals 8 cm dilation, 100% effacement, and –1 station. One hour later, despite
regular contractions occurring every 3 minutes, her cervical findings remain unchanged. On physical
examination, a triangular fontanelle is palpated posteriorly, and a diamond-shaped fontanelle is
palpated anteriorly. The fetal heart rate baseline is 140 beats per minute, with accelerations and no
decelerations. What is the most appropriate next step in managing this patient? Answer Choices: (A)
Artificial rupture of membranes (B) Administration of epidural anesthesia (C) Placement of the patient
in a hands-and-knees position (D) Administration of terbutaline (E) Lateral positioning of the patient (F)
Expectant management (G) Emergency cesarean delivery (H) Augmentation with oxytocin (I)
Application of vacuum extractor (J) Manual rotation
 A. Augmentation with oxytocin
B. Administration of terbutaline
C. Emergency cesarean delivery
D. Artificial rupture of membranes
E. Placement of the patient in a hands-and-knees position
F. Expectant management
G. Administration of epidural anesthesia
H. Application of vacuum extractor
I. Manual rotation
J. Lateral positioning of the patient
